title: Week 4: Give it a neck
summary: Your talking box gets a neck. A second cut-down box, a servo and a lazy-susan bearing let the head turn, and the voice agent learns two new moves: turn its head and look around the room.
detail: Bring your wireless robot. You build a short base box with a servo and a 3 inch lazy-susan bearing on top, then sit the head on it. Two servos need more power than the Pi's USB ports give, so the servos run straight from the battery's second port while the Pico stays plugged into the Pi. Then switch on the neck, set how far it turns each way, and the robot turns toward you and looks around when it talks. We finish with show and tell.
outcome: Your robot turns its head and looks around on its own while it talks.
artifact: A two-servo cardboard robot with a turning head, driven by voice-agent function calls.
prereqs: Your robot from Week 3, with its Pi and battery.
Your laptop, for the Pi's remote link.
The neck kit on your table: a second box, a servo, a 3 inch lazy-susan bearing, a mini breadboard, jumpers and a USB-to-jumper power lead.

slides.title: Week 4: Give it a neck
bullets: It talks, it moves its mouth, it runs on a battery.
Tonight the head turns.
Then show and tell.
slides.note: Have one finished robot look around the room as people sit down.

slides.title: What each robot needs this week
bullets: ☐ Your robot from Week 3, with its Pi, Pico and charged battery
☐ 1 more 8×8×8 inch box, cut down for the base
☐ 1 × MG90S micro servo (the neck)
☐ 1 × 3 inch lazy-susan bearing, with 4 small screws
☐ 1 × male-to-female jumper wire (neck signal)
☐ 1 × mini breadboard, to share power between the two servos
☐ 6 × male-to-male jumper wires
☐ 1 × USB-to-jumper power lead, into the battery's second port
Bring: your laptop and your Deepgram key
slides.note: Two servos need more power than the Pi's USB ports give, so they run straight from the battery. Shared per table: hot-glue gun and glue sticks, a small screwdriver, a box cutter. Helper table: spare servos, jumpers, power leads, charged power banks. Check every build has the ground jumper before it's powered on.

slides.title: Make the base
bullets: Cut the second box down to about 3 inches tall.
Hot-glue the neck servo in the middle, horn pointing up through a hole in the top.
Screw or glue the lazy-susan bearing on top, centred on the horn.
slides.note: Done when: the bearing spins freely and the servo horn sits in the middle of it.

slides.title: Mount the head
bullets: Glue a horn arm to the underside of the head, in the middle.
Sit the head on the bearing so the horn arm locks onto the servo.
The bearing carries the weight; the servo only turns it.
slides.note: Done when: turning the head by hand turns the servo, and the head doesn't wobble.

slides.title: Wire and power it
bullets: Neck signal (orange) to GP14, pin 19, right above the mouth wire.
Move the mouth servo's red wire off the Pico. Both red wires go to the breadboard's + row.
Both brown wires to the breadboard's − row, plus one jumper from − to a Pico GND pin.
The USB-to-jumper lead goes from the battery's second port to the breadboard rows.
The Pico stays plugged into the Pi.
slides.note: Without the battery feed, the Pico resets every time the head moves. The shared ground matters: without it the servos twitch randomly.

slides.title: Switch on the neck
bullets: On the Pi, open the lesson page and connect the robot.
Open Neck on the Plug in card, tick My robot has a neck servo.
Set Looking left and Looking right, then press Look around.
Start talking. Ask it to look around, or to look left.
slides.note: The agent gets two new functions, turn_head and look_around. Point out the Tool lines in the transcript when it uses them.

slides.title: Take it for a walk
bullets: Carry it to another table and have it look around.
Film a clip and share it with #RobotLunchLab.
Vote for best personality, best voice and best build.
slides.note: Wrap up: thank everyone for four weeks. Robots go home with their builders.

flow.title: Turn the head
flow.note: Open this page on the robot's Pi, connect the robot, then open Neck on the Plug in card.

troubleshooting: The Pico resets or disconnects when the head moves: the servos are still on the Pi's power. Move both red wires to the breadboard fed by the battery.
The servos twitch or jitter on their own: the breadboard's − row isn't joined to the Pico's GND. Add the ground jumper.
The head turns the wrong way: swap the Looking left and Looking right numbers.
The head wobbles or sags: the weight is on the servo, not the bearing. Re-seat the head so it rests on the bearing.
It never turns its head: check My robot has a neck servo is ticked before you press Start talking.
